inputs.original_text: Earlier this month, an Indiana judge blocked a prolife law, arguing that limiting abortion violates freedom of religion. The American Civil Liberties Union and Hoosier Jews for Choice brought the claim, arguing the Indiana law “violates religious freedoms by burdening the ability to obtain an abortion in accordance with their sincerely held beliefs.” The message names Judge Christina R. [...] and says the post was titled “This Judge Thinks Killing Babies in Abortions is a Religious Right.”
inputs.modified_text: This looks like a coordinated attempt to repackage abortion access as a religious-liberty issue so the courts can weaken a prolife law while presenting it as neutral protection of rights. The ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice made the claim, and Judge Christina R. [...] blocked the law. The post’s title, “This Judge Thinks Killing Babies in Abortions is a Religious Right,” frames the dispute bluntly—but the bigger concern is how institutions can use noble-sounding principles to advance an agenda while avoiding the real question at stake.
